newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine coco farmers oppose SanMig-Amatil deal.
newsitem.headline: Philippine coco farmers oppose SanMig-Amatil deal.

text.p: The National Coalition of Coconut Farmers' Organisation said on Monday it is opposing a deal recently entered into by Philippine food firm San Miguel Corp (SMC) and Coca-Cola Amatil of Australia over its local Coca-Cola operations.

"The coconut farmers as owners of the sequestered coconut levy funds in SMC, feel that the value of their shares in SMC ... have been unreasonably and radically reduced and that their control over their shares have been shifted away to a foreign company," the group said in a statement.
The group called for a renegotiation, saying that "something is wrong somewhere."
The statement was also signed by Philippine Coconut Authority administrator Virgilio David.
San Miguel recently signed a share swap deal with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil for its lucrative Coca-Cola bottling company.
Under the deal, San Miguel will give up its 70 percent control of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc in exchange for a 25 percent stake in the Australian company.
San Miguel shares plunged some 16 percent since the announcement but have subsequently recovered some ground.
The deal is expected to be finalised by June this year.
The coconut farmers own the coconut levy fund which in turn owns 51 percent of San Miguel but the voting rights are controlled by the government.
The levy fund was sequestered by the government on suspicion that it was used by business associates of former dictator Ferdinand Marcos to amass wealth.
Shareholders of San Miguel and Coca-Coca Amatil already approved the deal last month.
